subject: Hosting & migration follow-up — deployment options, constraints, and pilot proposal (Finlytics)

Subject: Hosting & migration follow-up — deployment options, constraints, and pilot proposal (Finlytics)

Hi Ariel — thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we stay aligned.

Summary of what I heard:
- Primary product use case: real-time document summarization + extraction inside Finlytics web app (user-facing).
- Latency requirement: ~150ms p50 for short prompts (<= 512 tokens); tolerate higher tail latency for long-form batch jobs.
- Steady throughput: ~25 requests/sec with predictable diurnal peaks (~2x) and occasional bursts up to 80 r/s for end-of-quarter jobs.
- Current stack: mix of a third-party LLM API (closed service) for day-to-day, and an internal legacy GPU cluster ("LegacyCluster") used for nightly batch runs and custom models.
- Security/compliance: SOC 2 required; data residency in US; key management with BYOK/HSM preferable.

Key constraints you mentioned:
1) Procurement timeline aims for a production decision in Q2 — predictable monthly cost is a high priority.
2) Some models are proprietary and currently live on LegacyCluster; the team expects to bring those weights along to avoid retraining.
3) Network/peering constraints — Finlytics requires VPC-level peering with strict IP allowlists, and we may need to route through customer-managed NAT.

Options we discussed (rough): Hosted API for quick POC -> Redwood Dedicated for predictable throughput and custom models -> Private (on-prem/VPC) if strict air-gap or full control needed.

Questions / asks (helps us size the pilot and produce a clean pilot SOW):
- Can you confirm which of the existing models you want to migrate (model names + format) and whether those are in TF/PyTorch/other?
- Do you have any required maintenance/downtime windows for migration?
- Are you able to provide a short network inventory (e.g., outbound IPs, firewall owners) so we can confirm VPC peering feasibility? I attached a one-page network requirements worksheet to make this easy (finlytics-network-reqs.xlsx).

Proposed next steps:
- Finlytics: share model inventory and network worksheet (this week if possible).
- Redwood: we will map out 2 feasible pilot tracks — (A) Hosted POC + Dedicated cutover, (B) Dedicated pilot with custom model onboarding — with effort/estimate and rollback plan.
- Align on pilot acceptance criteria (latency SLO, token cost target, migration timebox).

I'll loop in Aditya for the technical migration notes and Marissa on procurement/terms. If the above looks accurate, can we target a short follow-up next Tues/Wed (30 min) to confirm pilot track?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Thanks Kimberly — the recap is spot on. A few clarifications from our side:

- Preferred production mode: Dedicated capacity looks most attractive because we need predictable monthly spend and isolated GPU pools for our proprietary models. That said, we are open to starting with Hosted for a quick POC if that meaningfully shortens the timeline.
- Model inventory: most of the proprietary work is in PyTorch (checkpoint folders). We also have a couple of legacy Llama-1 forks sitting on LegacyCluster in a non-standard format. We need help converting those or guidance on retraining cost if conversion isn't feasible.
- BYOK/HSM: required for keys that encrypt PII-derived vectors.
- Migration constraints: minimal downtime is important; ideally we do a rolling migration and validate outputs against current baseline. Batch jobs can be moved in a maintenance window on weekends.

Questions for Redwood:
1) Can you confirm whether Dedicated supports customer-supplied model weights (we don't mean hosted shields — we mean bringing our own weights to a Dedicated pool)?
2) What typical timelines do you see for moving models off a legacy GPU cluster (LegacyCluster) and into Redwood Dedicated/Private?

Happy to share the model inventory and the completed network worksheet by EOD Wed.

Hi Ariel / Kim — quick technical note on the three deployment modes and the LegacyCluster migration path.

1) Hosted API (Redwood-managed):
- Pros: fastest path to POC; streaming and function-calling support out-of-the-box; Redwood can enable VPC peering and customer KMS (BYOK) in most regions for enterprise tenants.
- Cons: you cannot run arbitrary customer-supplied weights inside the standard hosted pool. We do support "hosted private tenancy" for some enterprise customers, but that usually looks like a short-term bridge.

2) Dedicated (reserved GPU pool):
- Pros: dedicated GPUs, predictable throughput and cost, support for custom model serving (bring-your-weights) depending on the chosen configuration. Can integrate with customer KMS and peering for data flows.
- Cons: longer lead time to provision GPUs and tune the serving profile; custom model onboarding requires storage + compatibility testing.

3) Private (VPC / on-prem):
- Pros: full control — on-prem or VPC-hosted control plane, HSM integrations, and support for air-gapped deployments. Supports arbitrary custom model weights and local-only data storage.
- Cons: largest up-front integration effort; different support model and licensing.

Migration notes for LegacyCluster migrations (typical steps & estimates):
- Inventory & format check (0.5–1 wk): confirm checkpoints, tokenizers, any custom kernel changes.
- Conversion & validation (1–3 wk): convert nonstandard formats to PyTorch/HF or quantized formats; re-run smoke tests and golden-output comparisons.
- Performance tuning & quantization (1–2 wk): choose quantization profile and test latency/throughput on target hardware.
- Pilot rollout & canary (1–2 wk): run canaries, compare outputs, and establish rollback.

Total ballpark: 3–6 weeks for most projects; edge cases (custom runtimes, undocumented model forks) can add more time.

Attachments: migration-checklist.md (checklist for the steps above)

If you share the model snapshot names and a sample target checkpoint (or a small artifact), we can run a quick compatibility check and give a tighter estimate. Happy to take that offline with whoever owns the LegacyCluster exports.

—Aditya
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
